Appeals court stands by LaMonica McIver ruling

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill last December.
  • LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., faced a setback Thursday in her effort to ditch charges tied to a scuffle during an oversight visit at an immigration detention facility last year, as a federal appeals court declined to reconsider its decision to let the case move forward.
  • Industry observers note that the decision by the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill last December. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Recent findings suggest that rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., faced a setback Thursday in her effort to ditch charges tied to a scuffle during an oversight visit at an immigration detention facility last year, as a federal appeals court declined to reconsider its decision to let the case move forward.

Industry observers note that the decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit leaves in place a 2-1 opinion from August which held that McIver was not immune from the charges, which stemmed from a confrontation between visiting members of Congress and federal agents while at the Delaney Hall facility in Newark. McIver has challenged the charges, arguing that her visit fell under the “speech or debate” immunity she has as a member of Congress because she was there to inspect detention conditions.

It has been revealed that in a statement McIver said she and her attorneys were looking at “every possible option” in response to the appeals court ruling. Her statement invoked the Trump administration’s threats to treat oversight efforts as criminal conduct and said “we are all one step closer to a world in which the president of the United States can try to imprison people simply because he does not like what they stand for.”.

“Donald Trump continues to send warning shots to Democrats in Congress and in all levels of power — but their case against me right now, in broad daylight, goes well beyond a warning. Because of a weaponized Department of Justice and because I dared to do my job and conduct oversight of ICE, I am facing 17 years in prison,” McIver said in her statement.

Following Thursday’s decision on rehearing, McIver could next ask the Supreme Court to weigh in on the case.

Recent findings suggest that the August majority opinion from Judge Cindy Chung, which Thursday’s decision leaves in place, said that two of the three charges against McIver did not fall under the immunity, which is limited to legislative acts. The majority sent the third charge back to the lower court for another ruling.

“We have considered the ‘nature’ of the charged conduct and concluded it is unambiguously non-legislative,” the judge wrote.

Recent findings suggest that separately, Judge Thomas Ambro partially dissented to offer a different approach to the case. Ambro would have required the trial judge to more closely examine the exact conduct McIver was charged with, as well as to examine whether the Trump administration targeted her because of her political views.

“I would allow her discovery into the truth of the matter — not only for her own sake but to safeguard the independence of our legislative bodies,” Ambro wrote.

Ambro did not vote on whether the full 3rd Circuit should rehear the case. Three judges voted to have the full 3rd Circuit hear McIver’s case, and Judge Emil Bove, a former Trump administration official and former personal attorney for the president, did not participate in the vote.

The criminal case started shortly after the Delaney Hall visit in May 2025, as prosecutors alleged that McIver assaulted federal agents during a scuffle around Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. Officials arrested Baraka that day and charged him with trespassing, but later dropped those charges.

Court filings in the case alleged that McIver struck agents during the confrontation. McIver has argued that she was effectively being charged for doing her job and federal agents were interfering with her attempts to inspect the facility.

Earlier this year, Judge Jamel K. Semper of the U.S. District Court for the District of Upcoming Jersey disagreed and ruled that the case could move forward.

Latest Update: Xiamen Airlines Places $7.4 Billion Order For 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8s Ahead Of Fresh Hub Move

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, xiamen Airlines has placed an order for 50 brand-newly introduced Boeing 737 MAX 8 narrowbody twinjets.
  • According to recent reports, this deal is the latest in a string of developments regarding Boeing's growth in China, which have defined the country's aviation landscape in 2026.
  • The deal still requires final government and shareholder approval, so it hasn't quite been finalized yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, xiamen Airlines has placed an order for 50 brand-newly introduced Boeing 737 MAX 8 narrowbody twinjets. The deal was confirmed in a November 24 stock exchange filing by China Southern Airlines, its parent company. The aircraft, which will be delivered from 2031 to 2034, have a total list price of $7.4 billion, although, as always, the airline will receive a bulk discount. They will support its forthcoming move to a new hub.

According to recent reports, this deal is the latest in a string of developments regarding Boeing's growth in China, which have defined the country's aviation landscape in 2026. Earlier this year, following a summit attended by both US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, China committed to buying 200 Boeing aircraft. It is unclear whether this deal is part of the total, but, either way, it marks a strong step forward.

The deal still requires final government and shareholder approval, so it hasn't quite been finalized yet. In any case, with the deliveries of these 50 upcoming narrowbody twinjet aircraft set to take place in batches between 2031 and 2034, there is plenty of time to get the finer details ironed out. China Southern cited "the relocation of [Xiamen Airlines'] operations to Xiamen Xiang’an International Airport" as a key factor.

Sources indicate that this airport is set to open next month, with the first phase able to handle 45 million passengers a year. China Southern added that the deal "supports the development of the hub network in Fujian, improves [Xiamen Airlines'] route network layout, and optimizes its fleet structure," and "complements the group’s recent purchase of Airbus aircraft." Commenting on Xiamen Airlines' fleet mix, China Southern remarked that:.

"Sourcing aircraft from different manufacturers will help diversify the group’s aircraft portfolio and enhance operational flexibility. The purchase will help strengthen the core competitiveness and sustainable development capabilities of the organization and Xiamen Airlines.".

It has been revealed that while relations between China and the US have been somewhat rocky over the years, Xiamen Airlines has long been a fan of Boeing's products. Until the arrival of its first Airbus jets in 2023, the carrier spent nearly 40 years as an all-Boeing airline from its founding in 1984. Its confidence in the manufacturer has been underlined by several other major deals, such as its purchase of ten 737-800s in 2016.

It has been revealed that boeing aircraft continue to dominate Xiamen Airlines' fleet today. According to data from ch-aviation, the carrier at the moment has just 25 Airbus jets at its disposal (eight A320neos and 17 A321neos), compared to 151 from Boeing. This figure consists of four 737-700s, 109 737-800s (including one freighter), 28 existing 737 MAX 8s, four 787-8s, and six 787-9s. It also has 12 more A320neos and 56 A321neos on order.

Given the 737-800's dominance at Xiamen Airlines, a growing portfolio of upcoming MAX 8 jets will ensure that this part of its operations has a natural successor. The type suits the carrier's domestic and regional operations, particularly when it comes to high-altitude flying out of certain Chinese airports. According to aeroLOPA, its existing MAX 8s have either 184 economy or eight business and 166 economy seats.

Things have been looking up for Boeing in China in 2026, not least on account of the 200-jet pledge that the country made following the Trump-Xi summit back in May. More recently, Reuters notes that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer mentioned in September there were "about 140" jetliner orders "in a good state", with 10 more being finalized. Trump said on Monday that he expects China to buy 250 more.

Found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

Another major coup for Boeing in China came in June, when it secured its first Chinese order for the 777-8F. This came as part of a wider $3.6 billion deal with China Southern Airlines, which committed to two 777-200Fs and five 777-8Fs (plus three options). However, rival builder Airbus has also seen success in China in recent years, with Air China having committed to buying six A350Fs in November 2025.

Sources indicate that listen closely, and you will notice that Ben Sasse uses the word “glorious” often. He uses it for the everyday goodness of Americans, the architecture of limited government they inherited, and now for his own rendezvous with God. Death by metastatic pancreatic cancer, Sasse says, is “what I need.”.

In a recent development, this historian by training, turnaround specialist by trade, former senator by a felt obligation, is the rare conservative undeterred by fatalism, even — especially — when staring it in the face. In wisdom tucked into a footnote in his second book, Sasse doesn’t deny that the world is a “broken place always at risk of spinning out of control.” It’s just that he finds this unruliness quieting in a way, and responds with “profound gratitude for the gifts we’ve received and consequently aims to conserve or preserve those blessings.”.

Sources indicate that john R. Puri is the Thomas L. Rhodes Fellow at National Review.

Latest Update: Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Collins took sole responsibility for a larger share of Maine earmarks.
  • After a bruising reelection defeat, Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, is ready to play hardball.
  • Eager to show how much she's delivered for her constituents, Collins took the lion's share of credit in her committee's fiscal 2027 spending bills for Maine earmarks — at the expense of her delegation colleague, independent Angus King, who caucuses with Democrats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Collins took sole responsibility for a larger share of Maine earmarks. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

After a bruising reelection defeat, Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, is ready to play hardball.

Eager to show how much she's delivered for her constituents, Collins took the lion's share of credit in her committee's fiscal 2027 spending bills for Maine earmarks — at the expense of her delegation colleague, independent Angus King, who caucuses with Democrats.

The amount of earmarks King secured fell dramatically compared to his previous year's total in Senate Appropriations Committee bills, as Collins took sole credit for most earmarks both senators had requested.

It has been revealed that the power play has instigated a dispute over how to award credit for "congressionally directed spending," better known as earmarks. It has also raised questions about a Senate rule that requires committee leaders to disclose the name of each senator who requested projects to be included in a spending bill before it can move on the floor.

According to recent reports, it’s undeniable that as the chair of the spending panel, Collins has more influence over which projects reach the final bills than her delegation mate. Collins spokesperson Phoebe Keller said that since available earmark funding is split into separate pots for the majority and minority to dole out, the bills reflect which of those funding sources was tapped to provide money to the relevant projects.

Keller stated that Collins deserves sole credit for the contested projects, as listed in the reports accompanying the bills.

"When only Collins is listed, it reflects only she chose to fund the project,” Keller noted.

A Democratic committee aide contested that characterization, saying that traditionally all requesters are named regardless of which party’s funding allocation is tapped for a project.

“The handling of these particular projects is a clear departure from the norm and will need to be rectified in conference negotiations,” the aide noted.

Sources indicate that king is credited with approximately $54 million in fiscal 2027 earmarks in the bills Collins released this month, including joint projects with Collins. That's down from around $231 million in the Senate's fiscal 2026 bills, according to a CQ Roll Call analysis.

Last year, King and Collins were both listed on 75 of the 77 projects that both requested that were included in the Senate bills, with just two carrying only Collins’ name. This year, Collins claimed sole responsibility for over $125 million in projects that both she and King requested, approximately two-thirds of the joint requests.

While King’s overall requests fell by more than $200 million this year versus last, his success in securing requested funds plummeted at a far greater rate with less credit for overlapping projects.

The joint requests for which Collins claimed sole credit include five for the Maine Department of Transportation in the Transportation-HUD bill, including $10.7 million for northern freight rail improvements; $9.6 million for Route 26 reconstruction in Oxford; and $7.2 million for improvements in Rockport, among others.

In the Labor-HHS-Education bill, projects Collins took sole credit for include $4 million for the University of Maine for biology laboratory equipment and just over $4 million for the creation of a modern emergency helipad at Lincoln Hospital.

And the Interior-Environment bill features $4 million each for wastewater improvements in Limestone and Kennebec that both Collins and King asked for but are only attributed to Collins, among others.

Similarly, the Agriculture, Commerce-Justice-Science and Homeland Security bills all include a project requested by both senators that only Collins is listed as securing in the bill.

The outgoing Appropriations chair’s ability to fuel billions of dollars in federal funding for her state during her career was the centerpiece of her ultimately unsuccessful campaign for reelection, which she lost to Democrat Troy Jackson.

As written, the draft bills appear to risk running afoul of a Senate rule that requires the committee’s chair to identify each senator who requested projects in a bill online at least 48 hours before a vote to advance the legislation on the floor.

The relevant rule, Senate Rule 44, states that it is out of order to vote on a motion to proceed to consider a bill unless the chairman of the committee certifies that “each congressionally directed spending item . . . has been identified through lists, charts, or other similar means including the name of each Senator who submitted a request to the committee for each item so identified.”.

That information must be “available on a publicly accessible congressional website in a searchable format at least 48 hours before such vote.”.

A King spokesman called on the spending panel to add his name to the relevant requests.

“We believe this must have been an oversight and assume the committee will enhancement the requests —per Senate rules — once it’s called to their attention,” King spokesman Matthew Felling remarked.

Sources indicate that the bills released by Collins are drafts, and no floor action on final fiscal 2027 spending bills is expected this Congress. There’s limited time left before the Dec. 11 spending deadline, when all current funding is set to expire, and Democrats want to wait to negotiate final bills until they retake majorities in both chambers next year.

But to comply with the rule, before the bills reach the floor the reports accompanying the bills, that includes the earmark tables, may have to be rewritten to list King on the contested projects, or the committee may need to disclose the information elsewhere online.

Both chambers unveiled stricter ethics guidelines surrounding earmarks in 2021 when the practice returned after a decade-long ban.

Peter Cohn contributed to this report.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight was the subject of a hijacking by one of its own pilots.
    • Sources indicate that just under two months after the attempted attack, a delegation of Israeli authority figures traveled to the UAE to meet with their Emirati counterparts and discuss the next steps regarding the resumption of flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv.
    • According to One Mile At A Time, the Israeli delegation attended presentations by Emirati authorities in Dubai, where the latter party detailed the new steps that it had put into action following the attempted hijacking in order to improve aviation security.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight was the subject of a hijacking by one of its own pilots. While his efforts were thwarted, with fellow flydubai pilots traveling on board the service able to regain control and divert the jet to Saudi Arabia, it prompted a strong response, with Israeli authorities banning the airline until at least mid-December. Now, however, the carrier has been granted approval to return.

    Sources indicate that just under two months after the attempted attack, a delegation of Israeli authority figures traveled to the UAE to meet with their Emirati counterparts and discuss the next steps regarding the resumption of flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv. This was, after all, a route that flydubai had previously served extensively. While its return is subject to clearance, the news marks a strong step forward for flydubai.

    According to One Mile At A Time, the Israeli delegation attended presentations by Emirati authorities in Dubai, where the latter party detailed the new steps that it had put into action following the attempted hijacking in order to improve aviation security. While the finer details have not yet been made public, the presentation was compelling enough for Transportation Minister Miri Regev to take action.

    Recent findings suggest that specifically, he and his ministry have now approved the resumption of flydubai flights between the United Arab Emirates and Israel, having previously barred the carrier until at least December 15, 2026. Israel's Transportation Ministry said that this was "subject to clearance from security authorities," and "a significant step toward restoring air connectivity between Israel and the UAE." flydubai told Simple Flying that:.

    Recent findings suggest that "We continue to work closely with the relevant authorities and look forward to resuming our flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv. Updates will be communicated on our official channels.".

    Should flydubai's flights to Tel Aviv resume in due course, this will be a key step forward for the airline as it regains access to what used to be one of its top destinations. According to The Times of Israel, the carrier used to operate as many as ten flights a day in each direction between Tel Aviv and Dubai. These served both point-to-point traffic and connecting itineraries serving destinations further afield in Asia.

    It has been revealed that of course, with Israel and the UAE both being sizeable aviation markets, flydubai is not the only carrier that had previously had a strong presence on routes between the two countries. For instance, The Times of Israel notes that "security challenges have also delayed Israeli airlines El Al, Arkia, and Israir from resuming flights to the UAE," leaving Etihad as the only airline right now linking the two countries.

    In the wake of the attack, Israel imposed stricter screening procedures regarding the crews operating flights that either serve destinations in the country or traverse its airspace. Elsewhere, The Times of Israel notes that UAE flag carrier Emirates has yet to resume its own flights from Dubai to Tel Aviv since Emirati authorities halted them in February after US and Israeli forces began their attacks on Iran.

    It was just under two months ago that the events of flydubai flight FZ1073 made headlines all around the world. While flying from Dubai International Airport (DXB) in the UAE to Tel Aviv Ben Gurion (TLV) in Israel, the flight's First Officer attacked the Captain with an axe and attempted to crash the plane, which descended sharply. After passengers fought off the attacker, deadheading pilots regained control.

    Recent findings suggest that the aircraft involved, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, descended more than 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds, prompting US President Donald Trump to praise the American planemaker on account of the jet having withstood forces "far beyond" its design. After diverting to Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Airport (TUU) in Saudi Arabia, the First Officer was taken into custody, with investigations revealing the full extent of his plans.

    • But banning trading by members of Congress may not be easy, and some worry the issue could get bogged down in larger debates over the party’s anti-corruption agenda.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, here at a news conference on Capitol Hill last week, says banning stock trading in Congress is a “high priority.” Now Democrats must decide what form their push will take. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    After stock trading became a major talking point on the campaign trail this fall, Democrats are feeling pressure to push through a bill in the upcoming year.

    But banning trading by members of Congress may not be easy, and some worry the issue could get bogged down in larger debates over the party’s anti-corruption agenda.

    According to recent reports, “I’d rather have it be a clean bill focused on stock trading, and not muddy it by adding other topics, even if they’re good policies,” said Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I.

    In a recent development, the incoming majority could plant a flag on government accountability with a broad package ranging from insider trading to campaign finance and more. Or they could zoom in on the stocks matter with a standalone bill.

    Magaziner said he hasn’t received any assurances from House Democratic leaders, instead describing a “collaborative conversation” about what form the legislation could take.

    “I worry that it would get weighed down under its own weight if you try to load it up with too many things,” Magaziner stated, while stressing he would support whatever expected incoming Speaker Hakeem Jeffries decides.

    Meanwhile, more than half of the Democrats in the incoming freshman class are calling for action on Day One of the newly introduced Congress, sending a letter to Jeffries last week suggesting they make a “down payment on much-needed reform” by changing House rules to curb stock trading.

    “Democrats may have won the election, but we have a long way to go to earn back the trust of voters across the country,” reads the letter, led by Reps.-elect Sarah Trone Garriott of Iowa and Jamie Ager of North Carolina. “A stock trading ban alone will not fix Washington, but it is the fastest way to show voters we heard them.”.

    Recent findings suggest that folding new language into the House’s internal rules would be a relatively easy path, requiring just a majority vote on the House floor, instead of passage in both chambers and the president’s signature. But such internal limits wouldn’t have the force of law, and some believe it would cool the urgency around the concern while doing little to crack down on insider trading.

    Recent findings suggest that colorado Rep. Jason Crow said moving forward promptly with a rule change wouldn’t preclude passing a bill, suggesting his fellow Democrats do both.

    In a recent development, “I want to pursue a parallel track,” remarked Crow, who co-chairs the End Corruption Caucus. “We want to move via rule and just prohibit it right out of the gate, or as much as we can.”.

    Jeffries has repeatedly remarked the topic is high on his to-do list as he looks to deliver on the accountability the “American people are demanding.”.

    “We’re committed to making sure we pass legislation that bans members of Congress from trading stocks. That will be a high priority,” he said at a news conference this week.

    But with more than two dozen different bills on the topic introduced over the past few years alone, lawmakers will have to decide exactly what a “ban” means to them.

    Recent findings suggest that some want to force members of Congress to fully offload their stocks with the exception of widely held mutual funds. Other proposals would block lawmakers from buying new stocks but allow them to keep the ones they already own, like a Republican-led bill that passed the House earlier this year but stalled in the Senate.

    Democrats resisted that push, which was led by outgoing House Administration Chair Bryan Steil, R-Wis., partly because it included an unrelated voter ID provision they called a “poison pill.” Many also complained the measure didn’t go far enough, extending to members’ spouses and dependent children but leaving out key figures in other branches of government, such as the president.

    It has been revealed that rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said she wants to stay close to the text of a consensus bill she hammered out last year with a small bipartisan group that included Magaziner and Reps. Chip Roy, R-Texas, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa.

    “That is the most comprehensive, thorough, thoughtful proposal and bipartisan proposal that we have,” she said of the bill, dubbed the Restore Trust in Congress Act.

    Industry observers note that that measure would not apply to President Donald Trump, as many Democrats have urged as they seek to draw attention to his ballooning wealth while in office. Still, Jayapal suggested a presidential stock trading ban could be moved separately.

    “There is discussion about the president, vice president, Cabinet, Supreme Court. I know we’re working on some language around enforcement, around those pieces, but I actually think that can be a separate bill,” Jayapal said. “We want to hold everyone accountable — but at minimum, we have to do ourselves.”.

    Sources indicate that it’s not clear how much appetite will exist next year for a bipartisan compromise that could realistically clear a 60-vote cloture threshold in the Senate. Notably, key Republicans who worked on the consensus bill will be leaving Congress, with Roy losing a primary bid for Texas attorney general and Fitzpatrick unseated by a Democratic challenger.

    While lawmakers could in theory advance a fresh stock-trading bill even sooner, before Democrats take control of both chambers, time and patience is short in the lame-duck session.

    At a news conference at the Capitol earlier this week with Crow and Jayapal, a group of freshman and returning Democrats took matters into their own hands, promising not to hold or trade individual stocks as part of a broader pledge backed by the Political Integrity Project.

    “My district, Upcoming York 10, happens to include Wall Street, but I don’t represent Wall Street. I represent the people of Brooklyn and Manhattan who deserve someone who goes to work every single day and shows right up front, ‘I work for you.’ And what better way to prove that than by day one showing we will ban members of Congress from enriching themselves, from trading stocks?” Rep.-elect Brad Lander noted.

    While momentum has grown in recent years as key senior lawmakers softened their resistance to a stock trading bill, not everyone is on board. Some members still argue, whether publicly or privately, that they should be able to trade on the stock market just like other citizens or that existing disclosure requirements established by a 2012 law are already enough to discourage dubious trades.

    Industry observers note that as they iron out the legislative text of any upcoming bill, members will have to decide how to handle emerging topics such as prediction markets and crypto, along with sticky questions such as whether to allow blind trusts. And extending restrictions to the president could be a nonstarter for many Republicans.

    Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., said Democrats in the next Congress should look to a bipartisan bill that advanced out of the Senate Homeland and Governmental Affairs Committee in July 2025 as a model.

    “The legislation we passed out of the committee applied to the executive branch,” he remarked. “But it didn’t take effect for anybody until their next terms, which was a compromise.”.

    That proposal would apply to future presidents but not the current one, potentially freeing up more Republicans to vote for it without angering Trump. Still, it hasn’t seen action on the Senate floor.

    Hawley remarked that while he’d like to see a “full ban on trading and holding” in Congress, he would be open to a weaker proposal in the interest of getting something done.

    “I’ll take anything that’s an incremental improvement over what we have now, which is nothing,” he stated.

    Aris Folley contributed to this report.

    #179949. Why Southwest Airlines Isn’t Rejecting Early Boeing 737 MAX 7s Like 777X Airlines Did

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1617 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Southwest Airlines Isn’t Rejecting Early Boeing 737 MAX 7s Like 777X Airlines Did

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that boeing's long-delayed 777X program has encountered an unusual problem: some of its largest customers do not want the aircraft it built first.
    • However, Southwest Airlines is taking a different approach with the Boeing 737 MAX 7.
    • In a recent development, emirates President Tim Clark confirmed in July that the airline would refuse delivery of its first ten Boeing 777Xs, citing the extensive modifications required to incorporate design changes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that boeing's long-delayed 777X program has encountered an unusual problem: some of its largest customers do not want the aircraft it built first. Emirates has rejected its earliest examples, while Lufthansa is negotiating over which aircraft it will accept. The issue is the extensive modifications necessary to bring older airframes up to current production standards, following years of development and certification delays.

    However, Southwest Airlines is taking a different approach with the Boeing 737 MAX 7. Following the aircraft's certification in August, the carrier is preparing to accept 27 previously manufactured examples that have spent years in storage. The contrasting responses raise an interesting question: why is Southwest willing to take aircraft built before certification when major 777X customers are rejecting theirs?

    In a recent development, emirates President Tim Clark confirmed in July that the airline would refuse delivery of its first ten Boeing 777Xs, citing the extensive modifications required to incorporate design changes. The airline subsequently revealed that it had informed Boeing of its decision approximately three years earlier. Clark reiterated his position during an October interview with Aviation Week, explaining that some aircraft had been sitting on their wheels since 2019:.

    Sources indicate that "We made it absolutely clear to Boeing some years ago that we won't be taking those, and that's both verbal and written to them. Our latest aircraft will be newly built.".

    Lufthansa has adopted a similar position, with CEO Carsten Spohr confirming in August that the German airline was negotiating with Boeing over its earliest 777-9s. Some would be rejected outright, while others might be accepted following modernization, provided Boeing contributed financially.

    The development followed concerns about accepting older-production aircraft, particularly given the extent of modifications accumulated during certification. The airline nevertheless continues to expect its first 777-9 deliveries in 2027. Boeing has approximately 30 completed early-production 777Xs requiring modifications.

    Industry observers note that on this front, CEO Kelly Ortberg acknowledged that the work could take years. The manufacturer faces the expensive task of updating aircraft manufactured before the design was finalized, with each aircraft being a bespoke project. Its latest financial filing specifically identifies modifications to completed aircraft among the program's larger risks.

    The MAX 7 first flew on March 16, 2018, with Boeing originally expecting certification and deliveries in 2019. However, the worldwide MAX grounding, heightened regulatory scrutiny, and subsequent technical problems repeatedly pushed back approval. Boeing eventually completed certification flight testing in July, more than eight years after the aircraft's maiden flight.

    The FAA subsequently certified the MAX 7 on August 3 following more than 1,000 hours of flight and ground testing. Regulators had required improvements to flight-control software, cockpit alerting, and the engine anti-ice system, addressing concerns that excessive heating could damage the engine inlet structure.

    Engine anti-ice redesign remains a major certification obstacle.

    Certification flight testing completed.

    First Southwest deliveries anticipated.

    Expected entry into passenger service.

    Boeing described certification as a major milestone for its smallest and longest-range MAX variant. Although certification allows Boeing to manufacture and deliver MAX 7s, Southwest must obtain separate operational approvals before carrying passengers.

    According to the airline's October financial filing, these include training updates, aircraft inspections, and validation flights with FAA representatives. Meanwhile, Boeing has deferred seeking European certification for the time being, reflecting the aircraft's overwhelmingly US-focused customer base.

    Despite the delays, Southwest is preparing to accept 27 MAX 7s that Boeing manufactured before certification. During September's Morgan Stanley Laguna Conference, CFO Tom Doxey explained that the airline had already spent approximately a year working with Boeing to update these aircraft. This confirms that the stored jets require modifications, although Southwest has not disclosed their cost or technical complexity. He said:.

    In a recent development, "I was up in Seattle a month ago for the sign-off for the MAX 7. That was really exciting. Of course, we're the largest customer, and we have 27 of those airplanes that are already built that have been in storage. We've been working with Boeing for a year now to be able to bring those to the current spec. That work is happening.".

    Industry observers note that so why is Southwest gladly accepting prebuilt MAX 7s when Emirates and Lufthansa have been quick to dismiss the prebuilt Boeing 777-9s? The difference lies partly in the programs themselves. The MAX 7 is a derivative of Boeing's established 737 family, whereas the 777X incorporates major changes including upcoming engines, composite wings, and folding wingtips.

    Updates to current specifications.

    Emirates rejecting; Lufthansa negotiating.

    Industry observers note that boeing's September 2026 filing identifies substantial engineering and change-incorporation risks to revision the prebuilt 777-9s, exacerbated by the size of the aircraft. While the existing MAX 7s will require some updates as well, they are nowhere near as substantial, so will cost less and can be completed more rapidly. Commercial considerations also matter, as Southwest is eager to get replacement aircraft.

    In a recent development, with over 440 737 MAX aircraft on firm order (and 130 options), it is well-positioned to negotiate the appropriate deal with Boeing to get the 27 aircraft delivery-ready, and Boeing is motivated to make it happen. By contrast, the 777X customers are negotiating over extremely expensive long-haul jets that are set to be flagship aircraft for decades to come, and after many years of delays, they hold all the cards and are far less inclined to be negotiable.

    Southwest's dependence on smaller Boeing 737s explains much of its commitment to the MAX 7. The airline presently operates 262 737-700s, averaging over 20 years old, alongside 188 737-800s and 356 MAX 8s. Unlike the major US network airlines, Southwest has no regional jet operation to handle smaller markets.

    In a recent development, as such, its 137-seat 737-700s are vital for serving thinner routes and maintaining frequency where larger aircraft would provide excessive capacity. Speaking on The Air Show podcast, COO Andrew Watterson explained that Southwest chose the MAX 7 over the Airbus A220 to preserve fleet and crew commonality. The aircraft also offers exceptional range and takeoff performance, making it especially suitable for higher altitude or hot weather departures:.

    Sources indicate that "We're excited about the MAX 7's performance on specific routes, such as from Las Vegas and Phoenix to Hawaii. It will be able to quite easily take off in the hotter part of the day and still make it to the islands without breaking a sweat.”.

    Watterson expects the first 27 MAX 7s to assume extended overwater duties that are right now supported by 28 specially equipped 737-800s, rather than exclusively replacing 737-700s. Southwest is increasingly concentrating services around major connecting stations.

    As such, the MAX 7 will remain valuable for thinner spokes and off-peak departures. However, Watterson acknowledged that the MAX 7 will probably represent a smaller proportion of Southwest's future fleet than originally envisaged, as its network strategy continues evolving.

    Industry observers note that southwest expects its first MAX 7 deliveries toward the end of 2026, followed by three to six months of operational preparation. Watterson suggested a spring-break introduction, while an internal rollout document reported by View From The Wing identifies March 2027 as the target.

    The process includes FAA validation and extended overwater approvals, meaning the first delivery will not immediately result in passenger service. Passengers will encounter a noticeably modernized aircraft. Southwest's MAX 7 layout features 150 RECARO seats, compared with 137 on its current 737-700s, representing a 9.5% capacity increase.

    The aircraft will also feature larger overhead bins, charging outlets, Starlink connectivity, and three lavatories rather than two. However, the airline's 2024 investor presentation specified 148 seats, so the latest arrangement represents a reported change. Not every improvement will be unique to the MAX 7.

    After all, Southwest introduced assigned seating in January, and is already retrofitting older aircraft with additional amenities. Its Starlink installation program is expected to reach the entire fleet by fall 2027. Nevertheless, the MAX 7 should offer passengers a more modern and consistent cabin from delivery, while providing Southwest with additional capacity and improved operating economics.

    Sources indicate that despite its certification, the MAX 7 has attracted remarkably few customers. Southwest held 240 firm orders as of October 22, 2026, alongside 130 options exercisable for either the MAX 7 or MAX 8. While the smaller variant offers a range of up to 3,800 nautical miles (4,373 miles; 7,040 km), most airlines favor larger narrowbodies that spread operating costs across more seats.

    Southwest's unusually large commitment makes it the aircraft's dominant customer. Other airlines have reconsidered their requirements. Luxair originally ordered four MAX 7s but subsequently shifted its commitments toward larger variants. Allegiant, which originally ordered 30, now favors the MAX 8.

    Original commitments shifted toward MAX 8; MAX 7 options remain a possibility.

    Original four commitments converted to larger variants.

    Earlier MAX 7 commitments; fleet strategy now emphasizes larger variants.

    Small historical commitments; current status unconfirmed.

    During its November earnings call, CFO BJ Neal explained that premium seating had weakened the smaller aircraft's economics relative to the MAX 8. The reality is that the economics are unforgiving, as a MAX 7 costs almost as much to operate as a MAX 8 once pilot salaries, airport fees, and fuel are included, yet it carries fewer people and has less space for premium seating.

    Ultimately, Southwest's willingness to accept its stored MAX 7s reflects a distinct set of operating requirements, rather than proof that those aircraft are unaffected by years of delays. The airline needs smaller, efficient jets while retaining its all-737 fleet model, although the final balance between MAX 7s and MAX 8s remains flexible. For Boeing, the contrasting responses of Southwest and its 777X customers demonstrate how certification delays can create very different commercial outcomes.

    Alaska Atmos Rewards Business Card Review: 90K Points & Strong Perks

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.
    • It has been revealed that the card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency.
    • Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. The card is issued by Bank of America, and is a rebranding of the former Alaska Airlines Visa Business Card.

    It has been revealed that the card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency. This post is my in-depth Atmos Rewards Business Card review, so I’d like to take a look at the card’s value proposition, for anyone who may be considering applying.

    Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.

    Before I get into my Atmos Rewards Business Card review, here’s a brief summary of the key details of the card:.

    Below are what I consider to be the pros and cons of the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem. To start, let’s cover the welcome bonus, card eligibility rules, annual fee, and more, since these are vital factors that cardmembers consider.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you’ll get 90,000 bonus points after you make $6,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. This is the best publicly available bonus that we’ve ever seen on the card, and you can find the bonus offer history in this post.

    In a recent development, based on my latest miles & points valuations, Atmos Rewards points are worth 1.5 cents each, given the great uses of these rewards. That means the 90,000 points are worth $1,350 for me.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is issued by Bank of America. The good news is that eligibility for this card is unrelated to having any other Atmos Rewards card, so you’re eligible for this card (including the bonus) if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card (learn more) or Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more).

    Let me emphasize that you are eligible for this product if you have any of the previously issued personal or business HawaiianMiles Barclays cards, or any of the previously issued personal Alaska Mileage Plan cards.

    Beyond that, Bank of America doesn’t have many consistent restrictions when it comes to getting approved for business cards. While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

    It has been revealed that there’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 limit, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

    I should also mention the following restriction in the terms:.

    I also understand that I may be declined for additional credit card accounts if my business entity right now has, or has had, another business card with Bank of America in the preceding 24 month period.

    Recent findings suggest that on the surface, this suggests you may be declined for a Bank of America business card if you have another Bank of America business card. However, anecdotally, this doesn’t appear to be enforced much. I think the term “may” is the key here (which is different than “will”).

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has a $195 annual fee. That’s on the steep side, though the card does have some premium perks. The good news is that you can add employee cards at no extra cost, so that annual fee covers the cost for all the cards you’ll have.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card has bonus categories that can help you rack up points faster. Furthermore, spending on the card can help you earn Atmos Rewards elite status. Let’s talk about how rewarding spending on the card can be.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 10x points per dollar spent on flights booked through the Atmos for Business website. If you’re looking to maximize your earning, this is where you want to book your Alaska and Hawaiian flights, as this is an incredible deal.

    You do need your own business to participate in the Atmos for Business program, and once registered, the return on spending is really tough to beat. Based on my valuation of points, that’s like an incremental 15% return on eligible airfare spending, on top of what you otherwise earn.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 3x points on all other eligible Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, with no caps. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 4.5% return on spending. So if you fly either of those Alaska Air Group carriers with any frequency, that’s a solid return on that spending.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 2x points on eligible dining purchases. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. It’s always nice to earn bonus points, though in fairness, 2x points isn’t exactly the biggest return on spending that we’ve seen.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 1x points on all other eligible spending. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. As you might expect, there are more exciting cards for everyday spending, as independently, that’s not a terribly exciting return.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card can help you earn elite status in the Atmos Rewards program. Specifically, the card offers one status point for every $3 in eligible spending. There’s no cap on how many status points you can earn with the card.

    If you are serious about earning status with spending, I’d recommend instead considering the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more), which offers one status point for every $2 in eligible spending.

    Beyond the ability to earn one status point per $3 spent, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers some additional threshold bonuses for spending, including bonus status points and discount codes:.

    Sources indicate that in other words, spending $200,000 per anniversary year would earn you 20,000 bonus status points, plus a discount code for 50% off a base fare. Just to cover the basics of that 50% off base fare discount code, here’s how that works:.

    Sources indicate that so the value of this will depend on how you’d usually travel, but this could easily save you many hundreds of dollars, depending on the type of ticket you book. It’s also still possible to upgrade these tickets, but at least the initial booking has to be in economy.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card also offers a Bank of America relationship bonus. If you have an eligible small business Bank of America checking or savings account, you’ll receive a bonus equal to 10% of the points you earn on each dollar spent.

    This is a way to earn even more rewards, as you’d earn 11x points on Atmos for Business purchases, 3.3x points on Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, 2.2x points on the other purchases eligible for bonus categories, and 1.1x points on everyday spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a decent card to use for purchases abroad, since you can rack up rewards without paying a fee.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a variety of benefits and credits, which can potentially more than justify the annual fee year after year. These perks are the main reason you want to consider picking up this card, in addition to the great welcome bonus. In no particular order, let’s go over the main benefits.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a free checked bag for you and up to six guests on the same reservation when flying on Alaska or Hawaiian. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized people on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card, so that’s a huge incentive to add authorized users to the card.

    Recent findings suggest that this is a great benefit that could save you a lot of money — Alaska and Hawaiian ordinarily charge $30-45 per checked bag, so that’s a savings of up to $90 per person roundtrip, if checking bags. If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian fairly often but don’t have elite status, that alone could rapidly more than justify the annual fee.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers preferred boarding for you and up to six guests on the same reservation. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized people on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card.

    This is a valuable benefit that helps you ensure that there’s space in the overhead bin for your bags. It’s also an awesome authorized user perk, so that you can share this benefit with others.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers four Alaska Lounge passes annually. The way this works, the primary cardmember will have one Alaska Lounge pass deposited into their Atmos Rewards account at the beginning of the quarter, valid through the end of the quarter.

    It has been revealed that each is valid for access to Alaska Lounges on a single calendar day, in conjunction with a same day flight operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, a oneworld airline, or an Alaska global partner. Each pass is valid for one adult, plus accompanying children. For what it’s worth, a day pass would otherwise cost $60 per person.

    In a recent development, if you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you can share your Atmos Rewards points with other members at no cost. The way this works, you can link your accounts with up to 10 other Atmos Rewards members (they don’t have to be family — accounts of friends are fine as well), and then you can move points back and forth for free.

    I’d argue that this is especially compelling for families, because it’s easier to rack up a sizable balance of points when you can consolidate them into one account.

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 20% back on Alaska and Hawaiian inflight purchases when paying with your card. This applies for the purchase of food, beverages, and Wi-Fi onboard flights, and the statement credit should post to your account within seven days. There’s no limit to how often you can take advantage of this.

    Industry observers note that let me just mention that Alaska and Hawaiian should have free Starlink Wi-Fi fleetwide by some point in 2027, at which point there won’t be savings anymore with Wi-Fi. That being said, it can still be used for food and beverages.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, then you’re eligible for a free same day confirmed flight change on Alaska. This ordinarily costs $50 per person, so that’s quite valuable.

    In a recent development, with this, you can change to another flight that might be more convenient, subject to capacity controls. This is especially useful in high frequency markets.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you’re eligible to receive a $50 voucher if you have an Alaska flight that is delayed by at least two hours, or that’s canceled within 24 hours of departure.

    The $50 voucher is valid for 48 hours, and will be delivered to the email address associated with the reservation, and can be used for food, drinks, etc. Travel must have been booked directly with Alaska using the eligible credit card.

    According to recent reports, those with the Atmos Rewards Business Card receive up to a $120 airport security credit every four years, in connection with TSA PreCheck or Global Entry. This is a perk offered by many premium credit cards, and there’s lots of value to this.

    Sources indicate that when talking about an Atmos Rewards credit card, it’s worth acknowledging the general value in earning and redeeming Atmos Rewards points. Alaska & Hawaiian are both in the oneworld alliance, and Atmos Rewards partners not only with oneworld partner airlines, but also with all kinds of other unaligned airlines. I consider Atmos Rewards to be one of the most valuable points currencies out there.

    Atmos Rewards has a distance based award chart, which varies a bit by region. For example, below is the one-way award chart within the Americas.

    It has been revealed that I constantly redeem Atmos Rewards points for travel within the United States, particularly on American. For example, all the time I redeem 4,500 points to fly one-way economy from Miami to Tampa (when cash fares would often be $200+), or 15,000 points to fly one-way business class from Miami to Chicago or New York (when cash fares would often be $500+). You simply can’t beat these redemption rates.

    The icing on the cake is that with Atmos Rewards, you earn status points for award flights, so those flights even count toward elite status, and that’s also why I’ve switched my business to Atmos Rewards.

    Of course there are lots of other opportunities with Atmos Rewards points as well. For example, I love the ability to redeem 75,000 points for one-way business class from the United States to many parts of Asia on carriers like Japan Airlines or Starlux Airlines — those are both awards that I’ve booked for myself in the past, and they were a great value.

    What makes this an even better value is that you can have a free stopover on a one-way award when traveling long haul. One thing worth being aware of is that Atmos Rewards has a $20 per person per direction partner award booking fee. However, that can be waived if you have the Atmos Rewards Summit Card.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, so how valuable is this product? A few thoughts….

    According to recent reports, first of all, I think there’s a lot of merit to picking up this card for the excellent welcome bonus, which includes a lot of points. The card also has significant ongoing benefits. The card also doesn’t count toward the Chase 5/24 limit, which is nice. Given the value of the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, there’s no reason not to pick up this card, if eligible.

    What about the long term value proposition of the card, though? If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency and don’t have elite status, the basic perks add up, including a first checked bag free, preferred boarding, a quarterly lounge pass, free points sharing, and more.

    However, I’d say there’s also merit to picking up one (or both) of the personal Atmos Rewards cards….

    The $395 annual fee Atmos Rewards Summit Card is the most premium Atmos Rewards credit card. While it’s a personal card, I still think it’s worth highlighting, as it’s incredibly lucrative. I’d take it a step further, and say that it’s my favorite airline credit card.

    Among other things, the card racks up status points at the fastest rate, the card allows you to earn Global Companion Awards, offers Alaska Lounge passes, enables free points sharing, waives partner award booking fees, offers 3x points on foreign purchases, and much more.

    If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency, then getting this card is an absolute no-brainer. As I see it, the anniversary 25K-point Global Companion Award alone basically justifies the annual fee, and that says nothing of all the other amazing perks.

    If you’re not set on an Atmos Rewards Business Card but want a dedicated business credit card that’s lucrative, there are some other great options that earn flexible points. Consider these if you want options for redeeming your rewards for more than just on Alaska, Hawaiian, and its partners:.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is an excellent business credit card that offers a massive welcome bonus and strong perks. The limited time welcome bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points will come in handy for cardmembers, and is more than enough reason to get the card.

    If you don’t yet have this card and are eligible, I’d highly recommend applying. This is a card that many people don’t have, yet which offers lots of value and a great bonus.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, and it runs parallel to the Atmos Rewards program (Atmos for Business used to be known as the EasyBiz program).

    Most major US airlines have a small business rewards program, and the intent is to offer extra rewards when businesses book travel. The good news is that even small businesses qualify for this, and it can really boost the rewards you earn.

    Industry observers note that along those lines, in light of the recent refresh of the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card (learn more), I think this program is worth a close look. Long story short, Atmos Rewards members could be earning up to 23.5x points per dollar spent on airfare. Based on my valuation of 1.5 cents per Atmos Rewards point, that’s the equivalent of a jaw dropping 35.25% return on eligible spending. That’s simply unrivaled.

    Atmos for Business is the self-managed business travel program by Alaska and Hawaiian, intended for small and medium sized businesses.

    The program is open to companies and organizations with at least $5,000 in annual travel spending, so if you’re a frequent flyer with the firm and have a small business, that’s not much of a hurdle. You can add an unlimited number of employees to your account, and all of their spending counts toward that requirement.

    Now, the terms suggest that you must have spent at least $5,000 or more on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian travel in the last 15 months, though in practice, that’s not directly enforced, best I can tell. After all, this is even intended to attract fresh businesses that may be looking to switch travel to Alaska or Hawaiian.

    It has been revealed that when a business enrolls in Atmos for Business, it’s assigned a company Atmos Rewards loyalty number. Atmos for Business then offers an impressive number of bonus rewards:.

    Beyond increased loyalty benefits for the business, Atmos for Business offers a platform that is supposed to make booking easier, with features like the following:.

    The total number of points that you can earn per dollar spent with Atmos for Business is pretty incredible, assuming you have the Atmos Rewards Business Card. As of 2027, Atmos Rewards members can choose how they get rewarded for flying, and they can choose to earn rewards based on distance flown, dollars spent, or segments flown.

    Assuming you choose to earn based on how much you spend, here’s how the math works out:.

    As you can see, a non-elite member booking through the Atmos for Business portal and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card would earn 15x points per dollar spent, while a Titanium member booking through the Atmos for Business portal and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card would earn 22.5x points.

    This doesn’t factor in the extra 1x points that the manufacturer earns, for a total of up to 23.5x points per dollar spent. Furthermore, it doesn’t factor in the 10% status points bonus, but that’s a different story.

    It has been revealed that while I’m going for top tier Atmos Rewards Titanium status, I still don’t fly with Alaska or Hawaiian often, given that I live in Miami, so it’s not the most practical carrier. Still, my goodness, the return on airfare spending is absolutely unreal here, if you are a loyalist.

    This included the country my business is registered in, my business name, my tax ID, my phone number, and my address.

    It was that easy, and I was registered instantly. The Atmos for Business program account management page looked mighty familiar, as it’s basically the same concept as the American AAdvantage Business program. There you can add travelers, manage payments, etc.

    To actually book travel, you just select the “Book Travel” heading. That will bring you to a search that looks identical to what you’ll find on Alaska’s website, but it’s customized to Atmos for Business.

    Pricing is identical to what you’d find directly on the websites of Alaska or Hawaiian, so that’s pretty tough to beat.

    Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. Even small businesses qualify, though the idea is that it’s for those who spend at least $5,000 per year on flights with the organization across employees, which isn’t a very high bar.

    The main advantage of Atmos for Business is that you earn one extra point per dollar spent, plus 10% bonus status points. But the area where the program gets really rewarding is if you have the Atmos Rewards Business Card, as that offers 10x points per dollar spent through Atmos for Business.

    If you were an Atmos Rewards Titanium member booking through Atmos for Business and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you’d potentially earn a total of 23.5x points per dollar spent on airfare, with no caps. This is simply an amazing rate of return. Man, I’m really bummed that I can’t fly with Alaska or Hawaiian more, as that return on spending is something to get excited about.

    At the Races: The latest Trump Democrats

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Editor’s note: At the Races will not publish next week on Thanksgiving Day.
    • By Niels Lesniewski, Mary Ellen McIntire and Daniela Altimari.
    • Senate Democrats powered their way to a majority by flipping nine seats – their biggest gain in nearly 70 years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Editor’s note: At the Races will not publish next week on Thanksgiving Day. We’ll be back the following week.

    By Niels Lesniewski, Mary Ellen McIntire and Daniela Altimari.

    Senate Democrats powered their way to a majority by flipping nine seats – their biggest gain in nearly 70 years.

    Eight of those wins were in states that Donald Trump has carried every time he’s run so it’s no surprise that some of the incoming senators are talking up the prospect of working with him over the next two years.

    Recent findings suggest that “We don't have time to wait until we have a different administration in the White House,” South Carolina Sen.-elect Annie Andrews told reporters this week. “We have two years ahead of us. We have very real problems that we need to address.”.

    Andrews is the first Democrat elected to the Senate from South Carolina since 1998. A pediatrician, she cited reducing prescription drug costs as a potential area of common ground with Trump.

    Recent findings suggest that “I support the president's attempts to stop taxes on tips and taxes on Social Security,” Andrews noted, citing two selling points of last year’s GOP reconciliation law. During the campaign, she issued a policy paper expressing support for making those provisions of the tax code permanent.

    James Talarico, the incoming senator from Texas, told fellow Democrats gathered in Denver last week that if Trump wanted “the same plaques and portraits and busts as LBJ, we can help make that a reality.”.

    Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    According to recent reports, according to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now. As an Italian hotel guest walked past him and attempted to enter an elevator, the American reportedly grabbed him and pulled him out.

Hotel staff called emergency services, and while first responders performed CPR, the American couldn’t be revived. Police also found an abrasion on the victim’s forehead.

    The Italian man remained at the scene, and told authorities that he had been acting in self-defense, after being attacked. Police took him into custody, and he potentially faces manslaughter charges, though the case is still being investigated.

    The hotel at which this incident happened hasn’t yet been named, but this occurred at Sukhumvit Soi 48 — there are several hotels in that area, with the biggest “brand name” property being a Ramada Plaza by Wyndham.

Bangkok is probably the one exception, where you see a countless number of people moving through lobbies, elevators, etc., engaged in various forms of “business.”.

While the man claims he was acting in self defense, he now potentially faces manslaughter charges.

    It’s really sad how people act sometimes. We only have one life to live, and how unfortunate to cut your life short so unnecessarily.

    Tech Report: What Are The World’s Tallest & Highest Hotels? The Answer Is Tricky…

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1350 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that there’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane.
    • The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume.
    • Sources indicate that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that there’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane. So, what are the tallest and highest hotels in the world? I want to talk about that in this post, and also discuss why the answer isn’t that straightforward.

    The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume. And even once we do define it, there’s the question of the extent to which the answer is actually useful. First let’s cover the distinction between the tallest hotel and the highest hotel.

    Sources indicate that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel. Most commonly, I see people suggest that this would include situations where at least 80% of the building is the hotel.

    This is different than the highest hotel, which would be the hotel that is highest above the ground, even if it only takes up a small percentage of a mixed-use building, where there might be apartments, residences, etc.

    In other words, a 50-story building that consists exclusively of a hotel would fall into the former category, while a 110-story building where the top 10 floors are a hotel would fall into the latter category.

    With that out of the way, let’s talk about the properties that are remarkable in these categories….

    According to recent reports, first, let’s cover some of the world’s tallest hotels. We’ll define this as hotels where at least 80% of the building consists of the hotel facility.

    It has been revealed that let me of course mention one downside of very tall standalone hotels — you could end up being on a very low floor. After all, if a high-rise consists exclusively (or almost exclusively) of hotel facilities, some people will end up on very low floors. The other downside, of course, is that these hotels are necessarily huge. If you prefer boutique hotels, you won’t find any on this list.

    Sources indicate that currently, the tallest hotel in the world is Ciel Tower Dubai. The 1,042-room hotel opened in 2024, rises to a height of 1,227 feet (374 meters), and has 82 floors.

    To go over the list of the top five tallest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, it’s interesting (but perhaps not surprising) that all four of the world’s tallest hotels are in Dubai.

    Industry observers note that the Conrad Shanghai, meanwhile, is located in the Shimao International Plaza, and this is the perfect example of how it’s tough to define what is technically the tallest. While the building it’s in rises to such a high height, roughly 25% of that height is the spire. So technically it’s a very tall building, but the usable space isn’t as high as you’d assume.

    Sources indicate that if you ask me, the world’s highest hotels are much more interesting than the world’s tallest hotels. That’s because the world’s highest hotels typically take up the top floors of some gravity-defying skyscrapers, and therefore, they can also be boutique properties.

    When defining the world’s tallest hotels, there are some general challenges:.

    Because of the above, there are some minor disagreements as to which hotel wins the title, but I’ll share my take (while acknowledging that I don’t have the ability to scale buildings with a measuring tape).

    According to recent reports, currently, the highest hotel is the Rosewood Guangzhou. The 251-room hotel opened in 2019, and it’s located at the top of the CTF Finance Centre Guangzhou, which reaches a height of 1,739 feet (530 meters).

    To go over the list of the top five highest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, those last two properties are kind of hard to judge, and particularly J Hotel Shanghai is tricky, given that the property is split between different parts of the building.

    It has been revealed that as the inverse of the above, I should mention that the Armani Hotel Dubai is located within the Burj Khalifa, which is the world’s tallest building. However, it’s located at the very bottom of the building, so that’s hardly that useful, for these purposes, since the hotel only goes as high as 39 floors.

    In a recent development, lastly, in the interest of being thorough, if we’re going to define a hotel as being “highest” based on the altitude above sea level, then we’d of course end up with a completely different list. Hotel Tayka del Desierto is located near the Salar de Uyuni salt flats in Bolivia. It’s at an altitude of 14,800 feet (4,500 meters), so it’s generally considered to be the highest up hotel in the world.

    I suppose depending on how we want to define “hotel,” there would probably be some simple guest houses at Everest Base Camp that go even higher, but I don’t think that’s within the spirit of what I’m trying to cover here.

    If you ask me, it’s always fun to stay in a hotel room that’s really high up. There’s an notable distinction between the tallest hotels and the highest hotels, though sometimes, the exact rankings are a bit blurred.

    While I’ve long been interested in this, I enjoyed researching this a bit more closely, and actually having a (sort of) definitive list. Ciel Tower Dubai is the world’s tallest hotel, while the Rosewood Guangzhou is the world’s highest hotel (unless you want to consider the 120th floor of the J Hotel Shanghai separately from the rest of the property).

    Have you stayed at any of the world’s tallest or highest hotels? Does it even hold any appeal to you?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that cathay Pacific has flown out of John F.
    • The shift to Terminal Six could cause friction for passengers hoping to connect onto a domestic flight within the US.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that cathay Pacific has flown out of John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)'s Terminal Eight for almost 30 years, yet in a few weeks' time it will be shifting over to Terminal Six. To mark the move, the Hong Kong carrier has looks to open its first lounge in Fresh York. The official moving date is set to be December 15.

    The shift to Terminal Six could cause friction for passengers hoping to connect onto a domestic flight within the US. American Airlines, Cathay's oneworld partner, is keeping its focus squarely on Terminal Eight. Such passengers will have to make the journey between the terminals.

    In a recent development, cathay first confirmed the move back in 2024. It stated that it would open a lounge during the move with a notable size at 10,000 square feet (930 square meters). Previously, premium passengers flying with Cathay Pacific have been directed to the Soho Lounge or the Greenwich Lounge operated by its partners in Terminal Eight. The former facility is available to Cathay first class ticket holders, and Cathay Diamond and oneworld Emerald members, along with one guest. The latter could be accessed by business class passengers.

    Sources indicate that british designer Ilse Crawford was involved in the ideation for the lounge. It will include a noodle bar, shower facilities, along with every type of modern power outlet. The lounge will also have a separate premium area created for first class and Cathay Diamond members.

    In a recent development, simple Flying has contacted Cathay for further comment. Cathay Pacific Senior Vice President, Americas Chris van den Hooven mentioned during the original 2024 announcement:.

    “This represents a huge milestone in Cathay Pacific’s 28 years of connecting New York with our home, Hong Kong and from 1 July it will be 20 years since we commenced our regular non-stop service. ​ It has long been our ambition to provide our customers a signature Cathay Pacific airport experience at JFK.".

    Along with being the first Cathay lounge in Latest York, it will also be the airline's second in the United States, with the first being at San Francisco International Airport (SFO), pictured above. Despite the opening date now just three weeks away, information on the exact features of the lounge is still lacking in detail. Cathay notes it will be at the "forefront of our lounge proposition.".

    In a recent development, the best indication of what premium passengers flying into New York can expect is revealed by a look at Cathay's SFO lounge, which opened in December 2011. The Instagram post embedded below reveals some of what passengers can find in this facility:.

    Cathay notes that this lounge gives passengers the ability to enjoy an "enticing range of food options", freshen up with the shower facilities, and stay productive in the work spaces. The showers include plush towels and premium amenities, while the working facilities have dividers to stop you from getting distracted by the busy airport atmosphere. Also included are luggage storage, disability access, and newspapers and magazines to pass the time before your flight.

    The upcoming lounge will mark Cathay's entrance into the newly opening Terminal Six. The facility has been built by JFK Millennium Partners. It forms part of a redevelopment by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey that has cost $19 billion.

    Other carriers that will operate there include the Star Alliance airlines, Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, and Brussels Airlines. The move is particularly significant for Cathay as it will be the only oneworld partner operating from the upcoming terminal, dislocating it from American Airlines. Passengers hoping to connect onto an American Airlines flight will now need to take the AirTrain between terminals, so they must make sure to allow additional time.

    • American Airlines offers a small business rewards program, known as the AAdvantage Business program.
